Title: PMS: What the Evidence Actually Supports

Description:
PMS mood symptoms are linked to a drop in allopregnanolone (a progesterone byproduct) during the luteal phase, while shifting aldosterone causes bloating. Calcium (about 1,200mg/day) has the strongest evidence for easing symptoms, vitamin B6 evidence is mixed with a safety caveat at high doses, and regular aerobic exercise consistently helps with fatigue and low mood.

If symptoms disrupt work or relationships most months, that may be PMDD — worth discussing with an OB-GYN.
